items.title: Ibovespa amplia série de altas com ajuda da Petrobras, apesar de Warsh
items.author: Paula Arend Laier
items.creator: Paula Arend Laier
items.summary: O Ibovespa fechou com um acréscimo modesto nesta sexta-feira, mas assegurou a oitava alta seguida, com Petrobras novamente entre os suportes.
items.body:
O Ibovespa fechou com um acréscimo modesto nesta sexta-feira, mas assegurou a oitava alta seguida, com Petrobras novamente entre os suportes.
Após ultrapassar os 176 mil pontos nos primeiros negócios, o índice perdeu força com declarações do chair do Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, de que o banco central dos Estados Unidos tem "trabalho a fazer” se a inflação na maior economia do mundo continuar acima de 2%.
A principal referência do mercado acionário brasileiro acabou terminando o dia com elevação de 0,3%, a 175.664,62 pontos, tendo marcado 176.420,61 na máxima e 173.893,63 na mínima da sessão. O volume financeiro somou R$21,8 bilhões.
Na semana, o Ibovespa acumulou uma alta de 2,71%, reduzindo a perda em agosto para 1,31%, conforme as informações preliminares. No ano, agora sobe 9,02%.
Em um discurso preparado para simpósio econômico do Fed em Jackson Hole, no Wyoming, Warsh afirmou que o BC norte-americano tem "[USN:L6N44P0RV TEXT:"trabalho a fazer"]” se os formuladores de política monetária não estiverem confiantes de que a inflação subjacente está voltando à meta de 2% da instituição.
“Este é o meu critério: devemos estar confiantes de que a inflação subjacente está caminhando em direção à nossa meta, de forma clara e com velocidade suficiente. Caso contrário, temos trabalho a fazer. Esse é o nosso trabalho... nosso mandato... e nossa responsabilidade”, afirmou.
Após a publicação da fala do titular do BC norte-americano, operadores [USN:L6N44P0S1 TEXT:"ampliaram"] as apostas em um aumento da taxa de juros em setembro nos EUA.
O S&P 500 (.SPX) , uma das referências do mercado acionário norte-americano, fechou com declínio de 0,25%. O título de 10 anos do Tesouro dos EUA registrava um rendimento de 4,724% no final da tarde, de 4,672% na véspera.
No Brasil, o último pregão da semana também mostrou que o país abriu 58.568 vagas formais de [USN:L1N44P0WA TEXT:"trabalho"] em julho, segundo dados do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged) divulgados pelo Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego, no pior resultado para o mês da série iniciada em 2020.
Números da B3 continuam mostrando entrada líquida de estrangeiros na bolsa paulista, com o saldo no último 26 positivo em R$1,3 bilhão, o quarto pregão seguido com fluxo positivo. No mês, o saldo segue negativo em R$18,7 bilhões.
DESTAQUES PETROBRAS PN e PETROBRAS ON (PETR3.SA) subiram 1,99% cada, resistindo à fraqueza dos preços do petróleo no exterior. Analistas do Bradesco BBI elevaram a recomendação dos papéis da estatal para "outperform", destacando que a recente queda das ações, impulsionada pela baixa dos preços do petróleo, combinada com o desempenho acima do esperado no crescimento da produção da companhia, resulta em uma relação risco versus retorno bastante favorável.
ITAÚ UNIBANCO PN fechou com variação positiva de 0,23%, em sessão que contou com dados de [USN:L1N44P0E1 TEXT:"crédito"] do Banco Central mostrando nova piora na inadimplência no país em julho. Fontes também afirmaram à Reuters que o BC está estudando uma série de [USN:L6N44P0VM TEXT:"medidas"] para conter o endividamento da população, mas planeja primeiro implementar limites para os bancos antes de se debruçar sobre um eventual teto para o comprometimento de renda das famílias com o pagamento de dívidas. No final do dia, BRADESCO PN subiu 0,89%, BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) apurou elevação de 1% e SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT valorizou-se 1,83%.
VALE ON (VALE3.SA) recuou 0,67%, apesar da alta dos futuros do [USN:L6N44P0N5 TEXT:"minério de ferro"] na China. A sexta-feira também contou com declarações do presidente-executivo da mineradora, Gustavo Pimenta, incluindo que está "otimista" com a possibilidade de edição de um decreto que trata das [USN:L1N44P0MV TEXT:"cavidades"] no setor de mineração, que poderia liberar investimentos ao tornar mais célere o licenciamento ambiental. Em paralelo, o ministro André Mendonça, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), pediu nesta sexta-feira destaque e suspendeu o [USN:L1N44P0R0 TEXT:"julgamento"] virtual sobre a cobrança de IRPJ e CSLL sobre lucros auferidos por controladas da companhia no exterior.
B3 ON (B3SA3.SA) subiu 1,97%, retomando a tendência postiva após uma pausa na véspera, que interrompeu uma série de quarto altas. Analistas do UBS BB reiteraram recomendação de compra para a ação em relatório publicado nesta semana, avaliando que a atividade de negociação pode continuar se recuperando no curto prazo à medida que o ciclo eleitoral se aproxima, com números de agosto já mais encorajadores. "Embora a visibilidade para os volumes negociados no médio prazo permaneça limitada, acreditamos que o preço atual da ação já incorpora parte das incertezas relacionadas ao cenário operacional futuro", afirmaram, citando ainda que também veem o papel com valuation atrativo.
MAGAZINE LUIZA ON (MGLU3.SA) caiu 4,55%, perdendo o fôlego após cinco altas seguidas, período em que acumulou uma valorização de quase 25%. No mês, o papel perde 8,15%, tendo de pano de fundo preocupações com a situação financeira no setor de varejo dado o ambiente macro desafiador, com juros em níveis elevados.
MRV&CO ON (MRVE3.SA) perdeu 5,12%, em pregão negativo para construtoras, tendo no radar a alta nas taxas dos contratos de DI. CYRELA ON (CYRE3.SA) fechou com declínio de 3,28%, também na ponta negativa do Ibovespa, tendo também no radar notícia envolvendo o memorando assinado pela companhia para venda de cerca de R$2,14 bi em ativos para TRX. O índice do setor imobiliário (.IMOB) na B3 recuou 0,89%.

items.title: Tribunal do Equador declara culpado ex-presidente Lenín Moreno em caso de corrupção
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Um tribunal do Equador declarou a responsabilidade do ex-presidente Lenín Moreno como autor direto do crime de suborno, em um caso de corrupção relacionado à construção de uma usina hidrelétrica, informou nesta sexta-feira a Procuradoria do país.
items.body:
Um tribunal do Equador declarou a responsabilidade do ex-presidente Lenín Moreno como autor direto do crime de suborno, em um caso de corrupção relacionado à construção de uma usina hidrelétrica, informou nesta sexta-feira a Procuradoria do país.
Durante a investigação, Moreno, de 73 anos, membros de sua família e parceiros comerciais locais e chineses foram associados a uma rede de corrupção ligada à construção da usina Coca Codo Sinclair, que começou a operar em 2016 e vem enfrentando problemas técnicos desde então.
O tribunal determinou que Moreno, valendo-se de sua condição de vice-presidente na época, tomou medidas para garantir a adjudicação do contrato para a construção da usina hidrelétrica — a maior do país andino — à empresa chinesa Sinohydro.
“A conduta de Lenín Moreno Garcés se enquadra nos termos da acusação formulada pela Procuradoria, crime de suborno atribuído ao servidor público na qualidade de autor direto”, afirmou o juiz relator Manuel Cabrera, durante a leitura da sentença.
A Procuradoria afirma, em sua investigação, que Moreno, em sua função de vice-presidente entre 2007 e 2013, juntamente com membros de sua família e amigos teriam recebido mais de US$1 milhão em propinas, configurando o crime de suborno.
A Sinohydro teria pago subornos no valor de US$76,1 milhões entre 2009 e 2018, que supostamente foram entregues em troca de falsos serviços de consultoria, segundo a investigação.
Posteriormente, segundo a Procuradoria, os pagamentos foram canalizados a partir de contas bancárias no exterior, por meio de uma “divisão percentual”, e transferidos para diversos paraísos fiscais e empresas de fachada ligadas ao mesmo núcleo familiar e empresarial.
“Não recebi nem um centavo da Sinohydro, então, por favor, não venham me dizer que sou acusado”, disse Moreno aos jornalistas. “Vim aqui para assumir minha responsabilidade, como homem de honra que sou, para provar minha inocência e a da minha família.”
Moreno, que também ocupou a Presidência do país entre 2017 e 2021, voltou ao país vindo do Paraguai, onde morou nos últimos anos, para enfrentar o julgamento.

items.title: Bond market may be pricing AI productivity gains as yields rise: JPMorgan Private Bank
items.author: Mehnaz Yasmin
items.creator: Mehnaz Yasmin
items.summary: Rising long-term bond yields may reflect investor expectations of an AI-driven productivity boom, rather than just concerns over inflation and swelling government debt, according to Jacob Manoukian, JPMorgan Private Bank’s U.S. head of investment strategy.
items.body:
Rising long-term bond yields may reflect investor expectations of an AI-driven productivity boom, rather than just concerns over inflation and swelling government debt, according to Jacob Manoukian, JPMorgan Private Bank’s U.S. head of investment strategy.
"The more positive interpretation of what the bond market is doing, which I think is getting a little bit less airtime among market participants, is this idea that the bond market might be sniffing out a little bit of a better productivity cycle from all the AI investment that's taking place," Manoukian told the Reuters Global Markets Forum on Thursday.
The optimism also extends to semiconductors, a major beneficiary of the AI investment cycle, where the firm remains bullish despite a more than 20% correction. But while the discount between two-year forward and trailing 12-month price-to-sales multiples for semiconductors has widened to 40%-50%, from a typical 20%, suggesting investors are already pricing in weaker earnings, Manoukian said this creates an opportunity for investors.
"We believe that a peak in earnings is already priced in, and we don't think that earnings have yet peaked. The opportunity for investors is that if some of these companies realize the sales that analysts have already forecasted, they could appreciate materially if the market is still willing to pay the same trailing-twelve-month earnings in 2028."
The AI investment boom is also fueling a borrowing spree among hyperscalers, adding to competition for funds at the long end of the bond market as they ramp up spending on data centers and other infrastructure.
AI-related debt issuance has topped [USN:L1N44G0HA TEXT:"$220 billion"] this year, double last year’s total, while U.S. corporate bond issuance has reached $1.68 trillion, up nearly 27% from the same period in 2025. That comes as Treasury yields have surged, with some investors arguing that the growing supply of corporate debt could increasingly crowd out demand for U.S. government bonds.
"AI-related issuance could be half of U.S. Treasury coupon issuance by the end of the year. So that's a material increase in global debt supply at the longer end of the curve," said Manoukian.
CARRY OVER DURATION: The combination of elevated long-term yields and uncertainty over where the long-end settles is also shaping JPMorgan Private Bank’s preference within fixed income, with the bank favoring carry from shorter-duration credit over outright duration exposure.
"We believe rates markets have turned too hawkish but that credit spreads offer attractive carry to buffer returns even if rate hikes lie ahead. We see attractive fundamental opportunities in extended credit," Manoukian said.
In the U.S., he favors bank preferreds, which can offer tax advantages through qualified dividend income treatment while sitting higher in the capital structure than common equity and providing a different return profile.
In Europe, he favors high-yield credit, pointing to relatively strong corporate fundamentals despite higher yields, rising government debt and energy-supply concerns.

items.title: Premiers at odds over leveraging potash in Canada's trade war with U.S.
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: Premiers are divided over whether to use Canada’s natural resources as leverage in the trade war with the U.S., and potash has emerged as a key point.
items.body: OTTAWA — Premiers are sharply divided over whether to use Canada’s natural resources as leverage in the trade war with the U.S., and potash has emerged as a key point of contention. Canada is a major global supplier of potash, a key ingredient in fertilizers that are vital for the agricultural sector. The U.S. imports about 85 per cent of its potash from Canada. While Ontario’s Doug Ford is pushing to pull the most damaging levers with the U.S., Saskatchewan’s Scott Moe and Alberta’s Danielle Smith are warning about a harmful long-term backlash. Federal politicians are also weighing in. NDP leader Avi Lewis called for an export tax on “oil, gas, thermal coal, potash and other minerals to hit Trump where it hurts.” Federal Green Party leader Elizabeth May agrees. “If you’re dealing with a really large bully who’s beating you up, you really need to get out your keys, put them between your fingers, and go for soft, fleshy parts that are gonna hurt,” she told The Canadian Press. “And that for us would be withholding potash.” At a news conference Wednesday, Ford said cutting the U.S. off from potash would kill the American agricultural sector “overnight.” But Moe, whose province supplies the U.S. with more than 86 per cent of the potash coming in from Canada, has said that such a move would backfire and harm Canadians. “That would be a tremendous economic hit to our province and to our nation,” Moe said at a news conference this week, warning of job losses and price hikes. He said Saskatchewan would not support any kind of export taxes or withholding supply, but did open the door to leveraging access to additional production in trade negotiations. “The United States of America, most assuredly, would switch to buying potash from other nations around the world. We would lose a long-term customer to some degree.” And while the drastically differing viewpoints of Ford and Moe may suggest cracks in the “Team Canada” approach that premiers and the prime minister have championed over the past year, one expert says it’s a matter of perspective. “Ontario and B.C., are the provinces that are going to be hit the most by the tariffs that Trump is rolling out,” said Jim Farney, the director and Stauffer Dunning chair at the School of Policy Studies at Queen’s University. He said he has seen some analysis suggesting Alberta and Saskatchewan will be “hardly touched” by the U.S. tariffs. Heather Exner-Pirot, a senior fellow and director of natural resources, energy and environment at the Macdonald-Laurier Institute, also said the tariff impact is “much more pungent” in places like Ontario with the auto and steel sectors being hit. “Out west, we don’t talk about CUSMA, we don’t talk about the tariffs. They’re a very small part of our lives and our economy, and we’re not getting damaged and it’s not really affecting us,” Exner-Pirot, who’s also an adviser with the Business Council of Canada, told The Canadian Press. “It is having such a different impact out West, and we don’t want it to have the same impact.” Taking questions from reporters Wednesday, Moe said one way to leverage natural resources in trade negotiations is to barter with “access to additional production” of potash, uranium and oil. But Exner-Pirot said such a move with potash might not make much of an impact. “In the United States, it’s not the growing market for potash. It’s pretty saturated. They use as much as they can use, and they’re efficient at it,” she said. She also said potash companies like Nutrien started stockpiling supply in the United States to get ahead of any potential tariffs or export taxes. “So when we say, ‘well, we’ll put an export tax on it,’ well, that won’t apply to what’s already there,” she said. Trump administration officials have repeatedly pointed out how the U.S. has not tariffed Canadian oil, energy, uranium and potash. White House officials have indicated there’s no intention at this point to change course. --- Nick Murray, The Canadian Press With files from Sarah Ritchie, and Kelly Geraldine Malone in Washington This report by The Canadian Press was first published Aug. 27, 2026.

items.title: Ex Mundialista Andrés Guardado integrará el cuerpo técnico de selección mexicana de fútbol
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El ex futbolista mexicano Andrés Guardado, quien disputó los Mundiales de 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 y 2022, será auxiliar técnico de Rafael Márquez en la selección de México para el proceso hacia la Copa del Mundo de 2030, informó el viernes la Federación local (FMF).
items.body:
El ex futbolista mexicano Andrés Guardado, quien disputó los Mundiales de 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 y 2022, será auxiliar técnico de Rafael Márquez en la selección de México para el proceso hacia la Copa del Mundo de 2030, informó el viernes la Federación local (FMF).
Además de Guardado, los españoles Juan Manuel Lillo, Vidal Paloma, Xabier Mancisidor y Pol Lorente conformarán el cuerpo técnico de la selección mexicana.
"Después de un Mundial 2026 que superó expectativas y generó una conexión importante entre el equipo y la afición, la selección nacional da a conocer el cuerpo técnico que Rafael Márquez conformó y encabezará durante su etapa al frente del equipo nacional y que estará integrado por Juan Manuel Lillo, Andrés Guardado y Vidal Paloma como auxiliares técnicos, Xabier Mancisidor como entrenador de porteros y Pol Lorente como preparador físico", informó la FMF en un comunicado.
"El cuerpo técnico reúne experiencia internacional, especialización y continuidad, distintas generaciones, escuelas y formas de trabajo, además de experiencia en competencias de élite como Copas del Mundo, UEFA Champions League, Premier League, LaLiga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Eredivisie y selecciones nacionales", agregó.
Como jugador, Guardado debutó en 2005 con Atlas, dos años después llegó al Deportivo La Coruña de España, país donde también militó en el Valencia y Real Betis, equipo con el que ganó la Copa del Rey en 2022.
Además, fue jugador del Bayer Leverkusen de Alemania y del PSV Eindhoven de Países Bajos, club con el que fue campeón en las temporadas 2014-2015 y 2015-2016, y con el que ganó la Supercopa en 2016 y 2017.
En enero de 2024 regresó a México para jugar con León, equipo con el que se retiró en 2025.
Además de los cinco Mundiales disputados, Guardado ganó con la selección de México la Copa Oro de la Concacaf en 2011, 2015 y 2019.
Tras su retiro como jugador, el llamado "Principito" comenzó a capacitarse como entrenador en Europa. Trabajó como auxiliar y técnico formativo en las categorías juveniles y la filial del Real Betis.
Márquez y su cuerpo técnico debutarán al frente de la selección mexicana el 26 de septiembre en un partido amistoso ante Colombia, y tres días después enfrentarán a Perú.
En octubre, el "Tri" -como llaman los mexicanos a su selección- jugará ante Estados Unidos y Chile.

items.title: From Roubaix to San Remo: Scot's race against the clock across cycling's five classics
items.author: Martyn Herman
items.creator: Martyn Herman
items.summary: Ultra cyclist James MacDonald's previous feats have often involved soul-destroying hours lapping velodromes but on Sunday the intrepid Scot sets out on a much more scenic record attempt.
items.body:
Ultra cyclist James MacDonald's previous feats have often involved soul-destroying hours lapping velodromes but on Sunday the intrepid Scot sets out on a much more scenic record attempt.
The Google software engineer plans to ride five of the toughest one-day races in professional cycling -- back-to-back in four days -- starting with the iconic 258km Paris-Roubaix.
He will then tackle the fabled cobbles of the 278km Tour of Flanders, followed by the Liege-Bastogne-Liege and Il Lombardia before finishing on Wednesday with the 298km Milan-San Remo.
In total MacDonald will cover a combined 1,349km across France, Belgium and Italy -- with his only rest coming during transfers between the different routes in the support vehicle.
"There's a big difference going from A to B instead of going round in circles," the 55-year-old MacDonald, whose bid to set a new indoor record for 100 miles was wrecked by illness at the London velodrome two years ago, told Reuters.
Riding the five so-called cycling Monuments back-to-back has never been officially done before so, however long it takes him, with transfer times included, it will set a benchmark for future challengers.
MacDonald has competed in endurance cycling events for more than 20 years. He once completed the 3,089-mile Race Across America as a solo rider in 2016, set the fastest recorded return time between John O' Groats and Land's End in 2017, and broke the indoor 100km record in 2021.
Last year, as a warm-up for his five monuments challenge, he added his third Guinness record for taking the shortest time to ride the 625km between Scotland's most distant points -- Mull of Galloway to John O' Groats.
DEFINING ONE-DAY RACES "Of all the challenges I have taken on, this feels like the one I have been building towards," MacDonald, who has spent two years planning the ride in conjunction with the World Ultra Cycling Association (WUCA), said.
"The Monuments are the defining one-day races in professional cycling, and nobody has attempted all five back-to-back in this format before. With the clock running continuously, every decision will matter, from how hard I push, when I sleep and how quickly the team can move me between routes."
The longest transfer will be from Liege down to Bergamo for Il Lombardia and one strict condition from WUCA is that a tracker ensures no speeding on the motorised sections.
"Those 10 hours off the bike (between Liege and Bergamo) will be tough, especially after 700km on the bike, that might feel awful," MacDonald said.
MacDonald has never ridden any of the five routes but says the weather forecast in France and Belgium could make it feel more like Scotland although riding the lumpy bergs of the Tour of Flanders at night could be disorientating.
But the roll down to the Mediterranean on the Ligurian Riviera will be something to look forward to.
"The pacing plan is that I'll hit the coast at sunrise. The profile for San Remo basically uphill and then it drops off a cliff as you get towards the Mediterranean."
Despite riding in Europe's culinary hot spots, MacDonald will not have time to indulge and will follow the advice of his nutritionists who are part of the support team led by challenge manager Matt Jones of Perpetual Sports Consulting.
"It's going to be pretty systematic for me," he said. "Energy gels, brioche buns, croissants, energy powders, chocolate milk. And lots of coffee."

By AJ Vicens and Raphael Satter
WASHINGTON, Aug 28 (Reuters) – U.S. officials are backpedaling on claims that several government agencies were hacked by Chinese spies, now saying that the organizations were among the hackers’ targets. 

In a freshly edited statement, the Justice Department said Friday that the U.S. Senate, the Federal Reserve, NASA, and others were “among the targets of QTFY,” a Chinese spy platform that officials called out on Wednesday during a internet domain seizure operation.

A previous version of statement said the government agencies had been among the hackers’ victims.

Show Full Article

A note left at the bottom of the newly edited statement said that “Edits have been made to ensure this press release accurately reflects the government’s allegations in the affidavit in support of the domain seizures.”

Reuters could not immediately establish which specific agencies the government now believed had been targeted and which ones had been breached. Messages seeking clarification from the Justice Department, the FBI, and CISA were not immediately returned on Friday.

items.title: Presos provisórios poderão votar em outubro; Bolsonaro não, pois cumpre pena
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Postagens nas redes sociais enganam ao afirmar que detentos não têm direito ao voto, pois presos provisórios poderão votar nas eleições deste ano. A nova lei que vedou a medida passará a valer apenas a partir do pleito de 2028.
items.body:
Postagens nas redes sociais enganam ao afirmar que detentos não têm direito ao voto, pois presos provisórios poderão votar nas eleições deste ano. A nova lei que vedou a medida passará a valer apenas a partir do pleito de 2028.
"O jeito mais irônico do bolsonarista saber que presidiário não vota: Bolsonaro está impedido de votar nas eleições de 2026, diz TSE", alega uma publicação no Threads com uma foto do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro.
Em dezembro de 2025, o Senado Federal aprovou o marco legal do combate ao crime organizado , que alterou o Código Eleitoral e passou a impedir o voto de presos provisórios (que aguardam julgamento).
Mesmo com a mudança, os presos provisórios ainda poderão votar nas eleições de outubro por determinação do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral ( TSE ), pois a nova lei foi aprovada menos de um ano antes do pleito.
O artigo 16 da Constituição diz que "a lei que alterar o processo eleitoral entrará em vigor na data de sua publicação, não se aplicando à eleição que ocorra até um ano da data de sua vigência".
Já Bolsonaro não poderá votar neste ano porque cumpre pena em prisão domiciliar , não sendo um preso provisório. O ex-presidente foi julgado e condenado por tentativa de golpe de Estado e outros crimes em setembro de 2025.
Bolsonaro perdeu seus direitos políticos , "enquanto durarem os efeitos da condenação criminal", com o trânsito em julgado da ação, em novembro do ano passado.
VEREDICTO Enganoso. Presos provisórios poderão votar nas eleições de 2026, por decisão do TSE. Já Bolsonaro está impedido porque sua condenação transitou em julgado.
Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

items.title: Cecafé revisa para cima dados parciais da exportação de agosto em 1,23 mi sacas
items.author: Marcelo Teixeira
items.creator: Marcelo Teixeira
items.summary: O Conselho dos Exportadores de Café do Brasil (Cecafé) revisou para cima seus dados preliminares sobre as exportações de agosto em 1,23 milhão de sacas de 60 kg, após constatar uma falha técnica que vinha reduzindo os números nos últimos dias, informou um representante da entidade à Reuters nesta sexta-feira.
items.body:
O Conselho dos Exportadores de Café do Brasil (Cecafé) revisou para cima seus dados preliminares sobre as exportações de agosto em 1,23 milhão de sacas de 60 kg, após constatar uma falha técnica que vinha reduzindo os números nos últimos dias, informou um representante da entidade à Reuters nesta sexta-feira.
Uma atualização automática nos sistemas do Cecafé para processar certificados de exportação -- um serviço que oferece ao mercado uma visão gradual do andamento dos embarques -- fez com que alguns dados fossem ignorados.
"Percebi que os números estavam atipicamente baixos para esta época do ano e solicitei a suspensão da divulgação dos dados até que realizássemos uma verificação completa", disse o diretor técnico do Cecafé, Eduardo Heron, à Reuters.
As verificações constataram que vários certificados de exportação do principal porto de exportação de café, em Santos, não estavam sendo contabilizados.
Como resultado das verificações e da correção dos sistemas, o volume preliminar de exportações de café, que era de 1,71 milhão de sacas em 24 de agosto, saltou para 2,94 milhões de sacas em 26 de agosto, informou o Cecafé.
Os futuros do café arábica na ICE caíram quase 4% no dia em que a revisão foi publicada no site do Cecafé.
"Acho que houve algum impacto nesta semana (devido à revisão)", disse um corretor de café sediado nos EUA.
Os preços do café arábica se recuperaram parcialmente na sexta-feira, registrando alta de 1%.
O Brasil é o maior exportador mundial e agosto é um mês crucial para os embarques, já que a colheita se aproxima do fim e os produtores vendem os grãos para o exterior.
items.raw_description: O Conselho dos Exportadores de Café do Brasil (Cecafé) revisou para cima seus dados preliminares sobre as exportações de agosto em 1,23 milhão de sacas de 60 kg, após constatar uma falha técnica que vinha reduzindo os números nos últimos dias, informou um representante da entidade à Reuters nesta sexta-feira.

items.summary:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞ 

上昇して取引を終えた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に反発。週間ベースでは０．０７％上昇した。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．１６％高と続伸し、週間では０．８９％上昇した。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のウォーシュ議長は米経済シンポジウム「ジャクソンホール会議」で講演し、基調的なインフレ率が目標の２％に向かっていると確信できなければ、ＦＲＢには「やるべき仕事がある」と述べた。この発言を受けて、市場では９月の米利上げ観測が強まった。

一方、イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）による年内の利上げ観測は後退した。

米イラン情勢に注目が集まる中、原油価格は軟調に推移し、北海ブレント先物は１バレル＝８９ドル前後で推移した。

エンジニアリング企業グッドウィンは好調な業績を示し、１．４％高。人材紹介会社のヘイズは５．１％高。パンミュア・リベラムが投資判断を引き上げ、買われた。

反発して取引を終えた。大統領選を控えて財政を巡る懸念から前日に下落したフランスのＣＡＣ４０指数は買い戻しが入り、０．９８％高。ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種指数は週間ベースで０．１５％高と、３週ぶりに反発した。

フランスの銀行クレディ・アグリコルは１．０％高。ＢＮＰパリバとソシエテ・ジェネラルはいずれも１．９％上昇した。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州高級品株１０種指数は１．９９％高。フランスの高級眼鏡大手、エシロールルックスオティカは自社株買い計画を発表し、２．４％上昇した。ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種石油・ガス株指数は０．３４％高。自動車・部品株指数は２．４８％上昇。ドイツの高級自動車大手ＢＭＷは４．５％値上がりした。

ドイツの１０年債利回りが１５年ぶりの高水準に上昇した。インフレの根強さと財政面での圧力に対する投資家の懸念が続いた。一方、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のウォーシュ議長は金利の見通しについて、より踏み込んだ発言を行った。nL6N44P0SC

もっとも、ウォーシュ議長の発言が欧州の債券に与えた影響は限定的で、市場の関心はイラン戦争がインフレや欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）の政策に及ぼす影響の継続的な行方に向いている。

ＥＣＢの金利見通しの変化に敏感な独２年債利回りは２．５ｂｐ上昇の２．８７３％。

トレーダーはＥＣＢの中銀預金金利について、２０２７年３月までに現行の２．２５％から２．８０％に達すると織り込んでいる。２７年終盤までにＥＣＢが３％まで利上げする確率は約６０％と、市場のプライシングは示唆している。

独１０年債利回りはほぼ横ばいの３．２５％。この日は一時、１５年ぶり高水準の３．２８５８％を付けた。

独仏スプレッドは８４．５ｂｐ。今後数カ月間、フランスが難航が予想される年次予算を巡る協議に直面する中、２４日には２０２４年１１月以来の高水準となる８６．６０ｂｐを記録していた。

items.summary: 03:49 PM EDT, 08/28/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Tech stocks were lower late Friday afternoon, with the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) falli
items.body: 03:49 PM EDT, 08/28/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Tech stocks were lower late Friday afternoon, with the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) falling 1.5% and the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) dropping 3.6%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was down 3.4%. In sector news, the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security is working on a slimmed-down replacement plan for the export controls on advanced AI chips that the Biden administration imposed to slow the technological progress of geopolitical rivals, The Information reported. The new rule is expected to close a loophole via which Chinese AI firms can access advanced chips through data centers in other countries, the report said. In corporate news, Marvell Technology (MRVL) shares fell past 9% after the company's stronger-than-expected fiscal Q2 results were overshadowed by investor concerns over the timing of revenue from its deal with Alphabet's (GOOGL, GOOG) Google. Workday (WDAY) raised the low end of its full-year subscription revenue outlook after the finance and human resources solutions provider recorded fiscal Q2 results above Wall Street's estimates. Its shares climbed past 6%. Amazon.com (AMZN) has signed a power purchase agreement in Germany and invested in four Swedish wind energy projects, the company said Friday. Amazon said it agreed to buy 600 megawatts of electricity from the planned Gennaker offshore wind farm in the Baltic Sea. Amazon shares rose 3.9%. Microsoft (MSFT) workers have raised concerns about the impact of its AI data centers on energy use, water consumption, emissions, and local communities, Bloomberg reported, citing Development Chief Noelle Walsh's memo to employees. Microsoft shares were up 1.7%.

items.title: ウクライナのフェドロフ前国防相、イタリア国防省顧問に就任へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ローマ ２８日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ローマ ２８日 ロイター] - イタリア国防省は２８日、ウクライナのフェドロフ前国防相がイタリア国防省のイノベーション顧問に就任すると発表した。

イタリアのクロセット国防相はフェドロフ氏について、軍事イノベーションを推進し、ロシアとの戦争でウクライナが主導権を取り戻す上で重要な役割を果たした人物と評価。イタリア国防省はフェドロフ氏が７月にウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領に更迭された直後に顧問就任を打診したと明らかにした。

フェドロフ氏は３５歳。Ｘへの投稿でクロセット氏の「個人的な支援」と顧問就任の提案に謝意を示し、「現代戦の技術導入や防衛産業の強化、新たな世界的安全保障上の課題への適応に向けて、イタリアを支援していく」とした。

items.title: CONSOLIDA Irã apela a países que não apliquem novas sanções dos EUA; mediadores se concentram na reabertura de Ormuz
items.author: Yasmine Ghania, Ahmed Tolba
items.creator: Yasmine Ghania, Ahmed Tolba
items.summary: O Irã condenou nesta sexta-feira as novas sanções econômicas dos Estados Unidos como “terrorismo de Estado”, enquanto seu líder supremo afirmou que estava proibindo atos que pudessem prejudicar a “coesão social”, em meio a preocupações de que mais dificuldades financeiras pudessem provocar agitação no país.
items.body:
O Irã condenou nesta sexta-feira as novas sanções econômicas dos Estados Unidos como “terrorismo de Estado”, enquanto seu líder supremo afirmou que estava proibindo atos que pudessem prejudicar a “coesão social”, em meio a preocupações de que mais dificuldades financeiras pudessem provocar agitação no país.
Com a guerra já completando seis meses e as negociações em um impasse, o governo do presidente Donald Trump intensificou os esforços para paralisar financeiramente o Irã, com o que chamou de “Dia D econômico”.
A onda de sanções agrava o impacto da guerra na economia iraniana, onde a inflação anual atingiu 66% no mês passado. O impasse em torno do Estreito de Ormuz continua sendo o maior ponto de tensão não resolvido do conflito.
Washington advertiu os países para que cortem seus laços comerciais com o Irã ou enfrentem sanções secundárias, embora o Departamento do Tesouro não tenha chegado a impor penalidades de fato.
O Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Irã afirmou em comunicado nesta sexta-feira que todos os países são obrigados, nos termos do direito internacional, a abster-se de aplicar as sanções dos EUA contra Teerã, acrescentando que a participação nessas sanções equivale a cumplicidade na imposição da vontade ilegal de um Estado sobre Estados independentes.
O ministério classificou as novas medidas dos EUA como um “crime contra a humanidade” que coloca a saúde e o sustento de milhões de civis em sério risco e exortou outras nações e órgãos da Organização das Nações Unidas a defenderem o Estado de Direito.
O líder supremo do Irã, o aiatolá Mojtaba Khamenei, que ficou ferido e não é visto em público desde o ataque de 28 de fevereiro que matou seu pai, afirmou em comunicado escrito nesta sexta-feira que havia proibido as autoridades de “cometer qualquer ato que prejudique a coesão social”.
Ele instou as autoridades a evitarem quaisquer “declarações desanimadoras que enfraqueçam a motivação nacional e pública”, em meio à preocupação entre os líderes iranianos de que mais pressão financeira sobre sua economia devastada pela guerra possa desencadear protestos.
Khamenei instou o governo a abordar seriamente os desafios econômicos e de subsistência, incluindo a inflação, o desemprego, os preços e a gestão dos mercados de bens e serviços.
NOVAS MEDIDAS VISAM BANCO EGÍPCIO Mais tarde nesta sexta-feira, uma autoridade norte-americana disse à Reuters que o governo Trump planeja impor restrições às filiais do Banque Misr do Egito nos Emirados Árabes Unidos por manterem relações comerciais com Teerã.
A autoridade afirmou que a regra proposta, se aprovada, retiraria do Banque Misr nos Emirados Árabes Unidos a capacidade de processar transações por meio de instituições financeiras dos EUA.
Autoridades do Tesouro anunciaram separadamente sanções contra uma entidade sediada em Hong Kong e uma pessoa ligada ao Banco Melli do Irã, de acordo com um comunicado publicado no site do departamento.
Enquanto os EUA se concentram em sua campanha de pressão econômica, outros têm buscado reativar os esforços diplomáticos para pôr fim à guerra.
Os mediadores têm pressionado pela reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz, que movimentava 20% do abastecimento mundial de petróleo antes do início da guerra, há seis meses, e cuja situação continua sendo o maior obstáculo a um acordo de paz.
O primeiro-ministro do Catar, xeque Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, afirmou ter enfatizado, durante conversas com líderes iranianos em Teerã na quinta-feira, a importância de retornar à situação pré-guerra de navegação livre pelo Estreito de Ormuz.
“PRESSÃO NÃO FUNCIONA”, DIZ IRÃ AOS EUA O ministro das Relações Exteriores do Irã, Abbas Araqchi, descreveu nesta sexta-feira as conversas com Al Thani como “criativas” e renovou seu apelo aos EUA para que parem de exercer pressão militar e econômica sobre seu país e retomem as negociações.
“Colocar a diplomacia de volta nos trilhos não é impossível. Depende da compreensão dos EUA de um fato simples: a pressão não funciona”, disse Araqchi no X.
O Catar, aliado dos EUA, e o Paquistão ajudaram a intermediar um memorando de entendimento em junho que levou a um cessar-fogo, mas que rapidamente se desfez devido a divergências entre o Irã e os EUA sobre o Estreito de Ormuz.
PODER DE BARGANHA DO IRÃ Depois que os EUA e Israel iniciaram a guerra em 28 de fevereiro, o Irã ameaçou atacar qualquer embarcação que transitasse pelo Estreito de Ormuz sem sua autorização, reduzindo o tráfego e elevando o preço do petróleo.
Os EUA insistem que o estreito continue sendo uma via navegável internacional aberta.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretário do Conselho Supremo de Segurança Nacional do Irã, disse na quinta-feira que o Irã estava preparando uma lista de condições para a reabertura do estreito. No passado, as condições do Irã incluíram o fim do bloqueio dos EUA aos portos iranianos, indenização e a retirada das sanções.
Comandantes militares dos EUA afirmam que as forças norte-americanas removeram do estreito as minas marítimas que haviam sido colocadas meses atrás pela Guarda Revolucionária Islâmica do Irã.
Trump afirmou repetidamente que o estreito está aberto, mas muitos navios optaram por não passar por ele devido às ameaças iranianas, e serviços de rastreamento de navios estimaram a atividade em cerca de 5% a 15% dos volumes normais.
Dados preliminares de tráfego marítimo divulgados nesta sexta-feira mostraram que apenas sete navios de carga transitaram pelo Estreito de Ormuz na quinta-feira, uma queda em relação aos 17 do dia anterior e abaixo da média de 15 nos últimos 10 dias.
No entanto, os preços do petróleo caíram nesta sexta-feira e caminhavam para uma queda semanal, em meio ao que analistas consideraram sinais de que mais petróleo estava fluindo pelo estreito, apesar do impasse diplomático, e de que os produtores estavam se adaptando cada vez mais às novas realidades na região do Golfo Pérsico.

items.title: Ecuador finds ex-President Moreno guilty in hydro plant bribery case
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: An Ecuadorean court found former President Lenin Moreno guilty on Friday in a bribery case tied to the construction of the Andean country's largest hydroelectric plant, the public prosecutor's office said.
items.body:
An Ecuadorean court found former President Lenin Moreno guilty on Friday in a bribery case tied to the construction of the Andean country's largest hydroelectric plant, the public prosecutor's office said.
The attorney general's office launched the investigation in March 2023, linking Moreno, family members and local and Chinese business partners, including Ecuador's former Chinese ambassador to Quito, to an alleged corruption network tied to the construction of the Coca Codo Sinclair plant, which began operating in 2016 and has experienced technical problems since.
"Lenin Moreno's conduct is consistent with the charges brought by the prosecution: the crime of bribery attributed to a public official," Judge Manuel Cabrera, head of the tribunal, said while delivering the ruling.
His wife and daughter were also found guilty.
Prosecutors had requested sentences of more than six years for Moreno and 19 other defendants. According to the attorney general's office, Sinohydro paid approximately $76.1 million in bribes between 2009 and 2018 through fraudulent consulting contracts.
Investigators alleged the funds were routed via overseas bank accounts and shell companies in tax havens to Moreno's family and business associates. The prosecution said Moreno and his close relatives received more than $1 million while he served as vice president from 2007 to 2013.
Moreno, 73, has consistently denied the allegations, maintaining he had no involvement in signing or overseeing the project's contracts.
"A word of advice to the prosecutor: you’re looking in the wrong place. Look at those who signed the contracts, at those who had the habit of demanding kickbacks, you’re looking in the wrong place," Moreno said at the hearing.
Moreno, who served as president from 2017 to 2021, returned to Ecuador from Paraguay to face the trial.

items.summary: Coco Gauff has had enough of the acquaintances who vanish for a year and resurface only when they want free tickets to see her compete in the U.S. Open.
items.body:
Coco Gauff has had enough of the acquaintances who vanish for a year and resurface only when they want free tickets to see her compete in the U.S. Open.
"To be honest, yeah, people come out of the woodwork. You haven't spoken to someone for years. They don't say congrats or happy birthday or nothing, then they're like, Oh, I'm in New York, can I have eight tickets to your match in your box, please," fourth seed Gauff told reporters on Friday.
Gauff's comments came a day after her mother posted a message on Instagram telling family and friends to stop asking for tickets, a post the two-time Grand Slam champion said she had no idea was coming but felt was overdue.
"I see this post, and I'm, like, Oh, my goodness. But honestly, it was needed, and it was directed, yeah, towards a few family and friends," said Gauff.
The Instagram post began with a "blunt, but necessary statement" saying her daughter's guest ticket requests for the U.S. Open had already been accounted for, before instructing friends and family to purchase their own tickets and never ask for more than two in future.
Gauff said she suspects a specific incident pushed her mother to finally speak out.
"I don't know who the person who sent her a text this year where she felt that was like the final straw. But somebody must have sent her something, and she was just, like, I need to make a post," said Gauff.
"Specifically in New York, it's just crazy. ... But some of the requests, you would be surprised at how absurd they are."
Gauff, who will face Turkey's Zeynep Sonmez in the first round of the U.S. Open, said she is happy to hand out tickets to those who genuinely support her, but that figuring out who falls into that category has become its own challenge.
"If you want to come, come. But I'm just, like, if I haven't heard from you all year and you hit me up, our last text is you hit me up for tickets, I don't know if you're there for -- because I do some things throughout the year," said Gauff.
"You can wish me happy birthday or something, so I think it's just trying to navigate those things."

items.title: Love, money & Dolly's financial legacy
items.author: Lauren Young
items.creator: Lauren Young
items.summary: From "9 to 5" to “Coat of Many Colors,” Dolly Parton's songs are filled with wisdom about work, worth and generosity.
items.body:
Combine love with money and you get a potent mix of romantic ideal and financial reality.
According to a recent WalletHub survey, modern couples are navigating everything from prenuptial agreements to secret bank accounts.
This week I spoke to Chip Lupo, an analyst with WalletHub, about the ways Americans are [USN:L6N44H16N TEXT:"tackling financial compatibility, privacy and shared budgets in today's complex economy"].
If you’ve got a significant other, I’d love to hear from you about the way you handle money. Do you share accounts? How do you divide up bills and expenses? Write to me via the link in my bio.
READ. WATCH. LISTEN. [USN:L1N44F0J6 TEXT:"Treasury yields are rising — why does it matter? "]
Is Nvidia’s dominance under threat?
[USN:L1N44L0V0 TEXT:"More US employers to drop weight-loss drugs in 2027, as healthcare costs increase "]
Why young people are investing in skills to lower future bills
When your bumper 401(k) is a tax problem waiting to happen
Can gold hit new highs again?
[USN:L6N44N0PI TEXT:"Fed's Warsh faces challenge whether inflation is a problem or not "]
[USN:L6N44I0Z8 TEXT:"Momentum, leveraged trading keep software stocks on roller coaster "]
[USN:L6N44F116 TEXT:"From Tokyo to London, heatwaves send men to work in shorts "]
What is a Treasury twist?
MONEY LESSONS FROM DOLLY PARTON [USN:L4N44N0LB TEXT:"As the world mourns"] the death of [USN:S0N44200S TEXT:"Dolly Parton"] this week, I have been thinking about her vast success — not only as a performer but as a businesswoman and philanthropist.
Parton certainly knew the struggles of poor people, after growing up in a cramped, one-room cabin in Tennessee's Smoky Mountains with her many siblings.
"I saw how my mom and dad struggled, and how they could stretch a dollar farther than you could begin to imagine,” [USN:KBN13O1R4 TEXT:"she told Reuters in this interview in 2016"]. “Even now, if I am thinking about spending a lot of money on clothing or furniture, I think 'I can't spend so much money on one thing; my poor old Daddy could have raised his family five years on that!' ”
Parton also said money is like the tide - it rolls in and it rolls out: “I often say I had to get rich in order to sing as if I was poor."
From "9 to 5" to “Coat of Many Colors,” her songs are filled with wisdom about work, worth and generosity.
Share the Dolly song that changed how you think about money. Write to me via the email address in my bio.
IS IT RISKY TO BET ON AN INDIVIDUAL STOCK? Some of the most sage advice I've ever heard is, "Don't put all of your eggs in one basket." And it's for a good reason — eggs are fragile and crack easily. The same can be said for equities.
I reached out to several certified financial planners and wealth advisers to get their take.
While their viewpoints diverge a bit, [USN:L6N44E0ZJ TEXT:"here is why"] concentrating your money in a single stock exposes you to significant risks.
A$K LAUREN I have lots of personal finance ideas, but the very best stories come from readers! What personal finance questions do you have about saving, spending, healthcare, credit and more? Write to me. I read every message!

items.title: The most hawkish Jackson Hole speech since 2009! Walsh's debut pushes the 2-year US Treasury yield up by more than 10 basis points
items.author: 华尔街见闻
items.creator: 华尔街见闻
items.summary: The yield on the two-year U.S. Treasury note surged more than 10 basis points intraday to a one-month high. Judging by the immediate rise in the two-year Treasury yield after the speech, the market reaction to Waller's remarks even exceeded that of Powell's Jackson Hole speeches in 2022 and 2023. The swaps market is now betting that the Federal Reserve may raise rates multiple times before July next year.
items.body: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Walsh's debut at the Jackson Hole annual meeting was quickly priced by the bond market as a strong hawkish signal. Walsh reiterated that the Fed's 2% PCE inflation target is "firm and fixed," and stated that if there isn't confidence that underlying inflation is falling toward the target in a "clear and sufficiently rapid" manner, then the Fed "still has work to do." Market data shows that the two-year US Treasury yield rose by over 10 basis points intraday, reaching a one-month high. At the same time, market pricing for a rate hike in September has noticeably intensified. According to Bloomberg's estimates, measured by the immediate rise in the two-year Treasury yield following the speech, Walsh's remarks may be the most hawkish since 2009, with market reaction even exceeding Powell's Jackson Hole speeches in 2022 and 2023. However, Walsh did not directly commit to a rate hike in September. The core of current market trading is a more hawkish policy function: if inflation continues to exceed the target and employment and the economy remain resilient, the Fed cannot rule out the possibility of further rate hikes. Two-Year Treasury “Voting”: Walsh’s Hawkishness Surpasses Powell’s 2022 and 2023 Speeches Bloomberg’s most notable assessment this time is to compare Walsh’s speech with past market reactions to previous Jackson Hole remarks. Measured by the immediate increase in the two-year Treasury yield after the speech, Walsh’s hawkish impact may be the strongest since 2009, even surpassing Powell’s speeches in 2022 and 2023. Of course, “most hawkish since 2009” here is based on the market response of the two-year Treasury yield, rather than an absolute rating of the speech text itself. Following Bernanke's speech in 2009, the two-year yield saw an even larger full-day increase. The two-year Treasury is highly sensitive to Fed policy rates, so its rapid rise indicates traders are raising their expectations for future short-term rates. Bloomberg notes that the swap market has already begun to price in the possibility that the Fed could hike rates several times before July 2027, suggesting that this may have reassured long-term bondholders concerned about inflation. “Short End Rises, Long End Stable”: US Treasury Yield Curve Shows Hawkish Distortion Following Walsh’s speech, the US Treasury market displayed a clear trend of short-end yields rising while the long-end remained relatively stable. Market data shows the two-year Treasury yield briefly rose above 4.35%, up about 12 basis points on the day; the 10-year yield climbed about 5 basis points to 4.72%; the 30-year yield’s increase was noticeably smaller. Walsh’s comments on inflation were the direct driver of the short-end yield rise. He stated: "We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving toward our goal, and that this process is both clear and sufficiently rapid. Otherwise, we still have work to do." He also said: "I find it hard to describe overall financial conditions as restrictive." These two statements together reinforced the market’s policy judgment: inflation is not yet fully under control, and financial conditions can hardly be described as restrictive, so the Fed may still need to further dampen demand through higher policy rates. Bloomberg Intelligence rate strategist Ira Jersey believes that Walsh's insistence on the 2% inflation target, resulting in a flatter yield curve, is a reasonable market response. However, if the Fed does not tighten policy in the next one or two meetings, this trend may reverse. In other words,the market has already priced in a more hawkish Walsh, but policy actions are needed next for confirmation. Stronger US Dollar, Weaker Gold: Market Awaits “More Work to Do” to Materialize Walsh’s hawkish comments also transmitted to the foreign exchange and precious metals markets. Bloomberg points out that while swap market pricing indicates the Fed, Bank of Japan, and European Central Bank could all hike rates in September, both the US dollar against the yen and the euro moved higher after Walsh's speech. Meanwhile, gold prices weakened. Previously, markets had increased their bets on a Fed rate hike in September, and with Walsh further solidifying his anti-inflation stance, the prospect of higher rates weighed on non-yielding assets like gold. Yet Walsh still did not provide a clear policy path for the September meeting. This remains the biggest uncertainty for markets:Walsh has provided a clear anti-inflation direction, but has not committed to specific timing of actions. If the Fed does not tighten policy in the next one or two FOMC meetings, the recent surge in short-end Treasury yields, the stronger dollar, and other market reactions could partially reverse; conversely, if inflation remains stubborn and the Fed does eventually hike rates, the hawkish pricing triggered by Walsh’s Jackson Hole speech could extend further. Therefore, for the market, what this Jackson Hole debut truly leaves behind is not a definitive signal of a September rate hike, but a clearer policy condition:If inflation doesn't fall fast enough, the Fed "still has work to do."

items.title: Feds say fake 49ers player swindled $1.3M from women
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Federal authorities claim a man posed as a San Francisco 49ers player and scammed more than two dozen women out of about $1.3 million.
items.body:
Federal authorities claim a man posed as a San Francisco 49ers player and scammed more than two dozen women out of about $1.3 million.
The FBI arrested Daejon Love, 35, and his alleged accomplice Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, on Aug. 24 in Boise, Idaho. They were charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud, according to the U.S. Attorney's office in the District of Oregon. The men remain in federal custody in Boise.
In a scheme that began in February 2022 and spanned more than four years until the Aug. 24 arrests, authorities say Love created fictitious personas to meet women on dating apps, presenting himself as a player for the Niners. To support that claim, he posted photos on social media wearing official team gear and posing with luxury vehicles.
The pair allegedly created fictitious investment opportunities to defraud 26 victims in California, Idaho, Washington and Oregon. The FBI believes there are "many more victims" out there.
"Love convinced many of the victims they were in sincere romantic relationships, that he was a sophisticated investor, and that Chan was his investment adviser who helped Love grow a fortune worth tens of millions of dollars," the U.S. Attorney's Office said in a statement.
"Love had romantic relationships with many of the victims and told them he wanted to build wealth and a future together. Love advertised nonexistent investment vehicles and claimed these investments would generate massive returns for both him and his victims."
None of the alleged victims interviewed said they received any return on their investments, or repayments for loans made to Love and Chan.
The U.S. Attorney's office said Love would block communications with the women after they ran out of funds to invest or asked too many questions.
--Field Level Media

items.title: How Does Wall Street View Waller and Jackson Hole Debut? Hawkish "Correction" of July Communication, No Rate Hike in September Could Further Harm Fed’s Credibility
items.author: 华尔街见闻
items.creator: 华尔街见闻
items.summary: The "New Fed News Agency" summarized that the Federal Reserve may not have finished its fight against inflation. The key points in Waller’s speech were that financial conditions are not restrictive and improvements in inflation are still insufficient. He did not provide a specific policy path, nor did he clearly indicate whether he supports a rate hike in September. In the U.S. Treasury market, the short end signals a need for a rate hike, while the long end remains more steady. Wall Street has not reached a consensus that a September rate increase is certain. Industry insiders believe Waller implied that the market should not expect a rate cut in the near term and should be prepared for a possible rate hike. However, while investors want GPS-level guidance, he only provided a compass, deliberately avoiding forward guidance—he spoke at length without offering substantial content.
items.body: Federal Reserve Chair Waller’s debut at the Jackson Hole annual meeting on Friday was widely interpreted by Wall Street as a hawkish “correction” to communications following the July FOMC meeting. Waller’s speech explicitly reiterated that the Fed’s 2% inflation target is non-negotiable, argued that current overall financial conditions are not clearly restrictive, and that the recent favorable PCE and CPI results are not enough to prove substantial improvement in underlying inflation trends. He stated bluntly that unless the Fed can be “clear and fast enough” that inflation is coming down, the Fed “still has work to do.” Reuters described this as Waller’s closest admission yet that further rate hikes may be needed. Waller’s statements quickly shifted Wall Street’s focus regarding the September FOMC meeting. Priya Misra, Head of Portfolio Strategy at JPMorgan Asset Management, directly called it a “hawkish speech,” viewing Waller as firmly reiterating the Fed’s commitment to price stability, and characterized it as a “clean-up” of the “communication error” from the July press conference. Aberdeen’s Director of Investments, Matthew Amis, warned that if the Fed does not hike rates in September, its credibility may suffer again. At the same time, institutions such as Wells Fargo and Fidelis Capital believe that Waller has left sufficient room for a near-term rate hike, although some also argue that he still hasn’t clearly presented the policy path for September. Nick Timiraos, the journalist dubbed the “new Fedwire,” noted the heart of the debate: Waller believes financial conditions are not restrictive, and recent improvements in inflation data have not convinced him that underlying trends have “meaningfully improved,” yet he has not provided a specific policy path nor explicitly stated whether he supports a September rate hike. Timiraos summarized Waller’s remarks as: the Fed may not be done fighting inflation. As a result, the market is facing a more hawkish policy diagnosis, but still lacks a clear “reaction function.” CME data shows that after Waller’s speech, the probability of a rate hike in September rose from around 35% before the speech to about 50%; other market metrics briefly showed probabilities rising further to nearly 60%. Hawkish Speech Restores Anti-Inflation Credibility The most immediate impact of Waller’s speech was the “correction” at the level of policy communication. JPMorgan Asset Management’s Priya Misra was very direct in her assessment of Waller’s remarks: “This was a hawkish speech.” She believed Waller was “strongly indicating” that policymakers are committed to price stability. Misra focused on the relationship between Waller’s speech and communication following the July FOMC meeting. She called Waller’s comments a forceful response to the “communication mishap” at the July press conference: “This is a strong response to what I saw as poor communication at the July press conference.” She even described it as a “clean-up act,” a corrective closure to July’s confusion. This view was echoed by other institutional figures as well. Christopher Hodge, Chief U.S. Economist at Natixis, believes Waller’s speech was a “clear improvement” over the July press conference. Previously, the market underestimated the likelihood of further rate hikes, but now market pricing is more reasonable. Hodge said Waller strengthened his anti-inflation credibility by directly acknowledging inflation problems, reaffirming the clear 2% target, and taking responsibility for the Fed’s institutional role on inflation. Nationwide’s Chief Market Strategist Mark Hackett thought Waller accomplished his goal: communicating his stance to the market without causing major disruption. Hackett pointed out that the market had previously misjudged, believing that the 2% inflation target might be softened, but Waller made it clear that this would not happen. “He is restating his hawkish stance more consistently, not abruptly escalating it.” Hackett summarized: Do not expect a rate cut soon; be prepared for hikes. The “New Fedwire” Highlights the Core: Financial Conditions Not Restrictive, Inflation Improvement Still Lacking Timiraos’ summary of Waller’s speech was even more focused on the policy judgment itself. He noted that Waller believes overall financial conditions are not restrictive; credit and loan markets show little sign of real constraint. Meanwhile, the recent inflation data has not convinced Waller that core trends have improved. Waller’s original statement: “I find it hard to describe overall financial conditions as restrictive.” Regarding recent inflation data, Waller said: “Though PCE and CPI figures over the summer were better than expected, that is not enough for me to believe underlying trends have shown meaningful improvement.” Timiraos highlighted this sentence both in his reports and on social media. In his view, this means the market cannot rely on recent better-than-expected inflation numbers to claim Waller has shifted towards a more dovish stance. What Waller really cares about is whether the core inflation trend is sustainably and sufficiently approaching the 2% target. Waller Gives a Compass, Not a GPS Another notable feature of Waller’s speech: he clearly told the market his policy principles, yet refuses to provide a specific policy reaction function. SEI Investments Chief Investment Officer Nathan Shetty believes that since Waller directly reiterated the firmness of the 2% PCE target, his speech can only be interpreted as more hawkish. But Ellen Hazen, Chief Market Strategist at F.L. Putnam Investment Management, pointed out that Waller did not disclose the Fed’s reaction function, leaving the market still in a “black box.” Waller explained that revealing too much about the policy reaction function might constrain the Fed, much as excessive forward guidance did in 2021. Hazen believes this means Waller wants to preserve greater flexibility for the Fed in responding to economic changes, but the market may not like this approach. Peter Andersen, founder of Andersen Capital, described it vividly: Investors want a GPS, but the Fed is offering only a compass. In his view, investors want Waller to detail the economic outlook and policy path, but Waller is actually telling the market: the “new Fed” will not offer as much explicit forward guidance as past chairs; markets must adapt to this “new regime.” “If There’s No Hike in September, Credibility Takes Another Hit”: Wall Street Bets on Near-Term Action Again For markets, the most significant change is that a September hike is once again at the core of the discussion. Aberdeen’s Matthew Amis believes Waller’s speech set up a crucial scenario for the September meeting: “If they don’t hike, their credibility takes another punch.” This links Waller’s anti-inflation stance to policy action in September: since he has made clear that core inflation must fall quickly enough, or the Fed “still has work to do,” if data does not improve but there is no hike in September, the market may begin to doubt the policy weight of Waller’s preceding hawkish statements. Wells Fargo Investment Institute’s Global Strategist Gary Schlossberg also believes Waller, though not explicit, has sent signals—“connecting all the dots”—of at least one, and possibly more, rate hikes ahead. He said inflation is unlikely to fall notably—something he does not expect—and that pressure may even increase over the next 6 to 8 months. Even if there is no hike in September, he expects the Fed is likely to act later this year. Chris Gunster, Head of Fixed Income at Fidelis Capital, said outright that the market now sees the probability of a September rate hike above 50%. He argued that Waller referenced several factors—elevated inflation, a strong job market, and economic resilience—that together leave the Fed with policy space for a near-term hike. “Short End Calls for Hikes, Long End Stays Calm”: The Market Turns Waller’s Diagnosis into Trade After Waller spoke, the U.S. Treasury market reacted swiftly, especially at the short end. Reuters reported that two-year Treasury yields rose as much as 11bps to 4.34%, a one-month high; ten-year yields were up 5bps to 4.72%, with the thirty-year rising significantly less. This reveal is the market’s take on Waller’s remarks: traders are raising their pricing of near-term policy rate hikes. Michael Rosen argued that short-end Treasuries dropped and long-end yields rose, showing the market is reassessing the Fed’s policy direction—a Fed seeing inflation as the primary risk means short-term rates could climb further. Fidelis Capital’s Gunster also pointed out that short-term yields rose while long-term yields fell, making the yield curve flatter, which is consistent with markets betting on Fed hikes. However, this market reaction does not mean Wall Street has reached a consensus that a September hike is certain. Peter Cardillo, Chief Market Economist at Spartan Capital, thinks the Fed is unlikely to act in September. He believes Waller acknowledged some summer improvement in inflation, though “not yet convincing,” so the Fed may want to wait and see the inflation prints for September and October before deciding to act. In other words, the market is repricing for hikes, but data remains the ultimate gatekeeper for whether a hike will actually happen in September. Waller Still Deliberately Avoids Forward Guidance: “Said a Lot, But No Substance” Not all institutions believe Waller’s remarks have fully repaired the policy communication issues. Eugene Epstein, Head of Trading and Structured Products at Moneycorp, felt that while Waller’s speech was initially hawkish, the substance was still limited. His assessment was very pointed: “Waller said a lot, but there doesn’t seem to be much real content.” Epstein noted that Waller has sent similar hawkish signals ahead of past FOMC meetings, but policy action did not always follow. He worries the market could again be “driven by hawkish rhetoric, only to find no actual policy change” afterward. Harris Financial Group Managing Partner Jamie Cox described this style as: “Waller said a lot but actually said nothing.” He sees Waller as trying to follow a middle path, both strengthening the anti-inflation commitment and refusing to constrain future policy with forward guidance. This is precisely where the “compass not GPS” metaphor fits best: Waller is willing to tell the market what kinds of data would provoke Fed action, but not which specific meetings would see action. The Real Risk of “No Hike in September”: Not Policy, but Credibility Summing up Wall Street commentary, what matters most from Waller’s speech is not that he has promised a September hike, but that he has reestablished a more hawkish policy logic: If employment is still robust, the economy resilient, and core inflation not falling fast enough toward 2%, then current financial conditions may not be restrictive and the Fed should not rule out higher policy rates. That’s why Amis thinks if there’s no September hike, Fed credibility could take a further hit. On the other hand, Cardillo, Epstein and others remind markets: hawkish talk does not equal policy decisions. Waller still sticks to his principle of “no forward guidance,” making no clear commitment to a September hike, nor offering a mechanical policy reaction function. Thus, perhaps the more accurate Wall Street consensus is: Waller has used his Jackson Hole speech to correct July’s communication with a hawkish tone; the odds of a September hike have risen—but whether it happens ultimately depends on employment and inflation data to come. As for Waller, the real policy test is shifting from “does the market understand what he’s saying,” to a more direct question: If the data doesn’t improve significantly, is he truly willing to turn this hawkish assessment into an actual September rate hike.

He did not provide a specific policy path, nor did he clearly indicate whether he supports a rate hike in September. In the U.S. Treasury market, the short end signals a need for a rate hike, while the long end remains more steady. Wall Street has not reached a consensus that a September rate increase is certain. Industry insiders believe Waller implied that the market should not expect a rate cut in the near term and should be prepared for a possible rate hike. However, while investors want GPS-level guidance, he only provided a compass, deliberately avoiding forward guidance—he spoke at length without offering substantial content.

items.title: Grupo de ransomware diz ter roubado dados de Berlim e põe em leilão
items.author: Maria Martinez, A.J. Vicens
items.creator: Maria Martinez, A.J. Vicens
items.summary: Um grupo de ransomware anunciou nesta sexta-feira que abriu leilão de uma grande quantidade de dados que roubou de órgãos públicos de Berlim, e as autoridades municipais da cidade alemã se recusaram a pagar.
items.body:
Um grupo de ransomware anunciou nesta sexta-feira que abriu leilão de uma grande quantidade de dados que roubou de órgãos públicos de Berlim, e as autoridades municipais da cidade alemã se recusaram a pagar.
O grupo Rhysida, que segundo pesquisadores opera a partir da Rússia ou da Europa Oriental, informou em seu site que roubou 5,79 terabytes de dados, incluindo 46.500 contratos, além de emails, números de telefone, senhas e informações confidenciais.
O grupo anunciou um leilão dos dados a um preço inicial de 30 bitcoins com duração de pouco menos de sete dias, exibindo uma contagem regressiva em seu site. O bitcoin era negociado a US$77.650 nesta sexta-feira.
O ataque hacker contra Berlim ocorre menos de um mês antes das eleições que a cidade-estado realizará em 20 de setembro.
“BERLIM NÃO SE SUBMETERÁ À EXTORSÃO” A emissora RBB informou na noite de quinta-feira que Berlim recebeu pedidos de resgate, mas não divulgou o valor.
“O estado de Berlim não se submeterá à extorsão”, afirmaram o prefeito de Berlim, Kai Wegner, e a senadora do Interior de Berlim, Iris Spranger, em comunicado conjunto nesta sexta-feira, antes que o grupo de ransomware reivindicasse o ataque em seu site.
As autoridades não puderam fornecer detalhes sobre o conteúdo ou o escopo dos dados afetados, pois a extensão da violação ainda estava sendo avaliada, disse Wegner a jornalistas.
Spranger disse que a infraestrutura eleitoral da cidade não foi afetada e que, segundo autoridades de segurança, nenhum dado relacionado à eleição havia sido comprometido.
RANSOMWARE O Rhysida assumiu a autoria de quase 280 ataques desde que surgiu em junho de 2023, de acordo com a plataforma de pesquisa sobre crimes cibernéticos eCrime.ch.
Aproximadamente metade das vítimas está nos EUA, seguidos pelo Reino Unido, Canadá e Itália, além de outros países, de acordo com o Ransom-DB, um serviço de análise e rastreamento de ransomware.
O grupo tem repetidamente tido como alvo instituições governamentais, como no caso do ataque de outubro de 2023 à British Library. O grupo também assumiu a autoria de ataques ao Exército chileno, escolas, unidades de saúde e empresas de todos os portes.

items.title: US officials revise claims that government agencies were hacked by Chinese, now say they were targets
items.author: A.J. Vicens, Raphael Satter
items.creator: A.J. Vicens, Raphael Satter
items.summary: U.S. officials are correcting earlier statements that several government agencies were hacked by Chinese hackers, now saying that the organizations were among the hackers' targets.
items.body:
U.S. officials are correcting earlier statements that several government agencies [USN:FWN44N10S TEXT:"were hacked by Chinese hackers"], now saying that the organizations were among the hackers' targets.
In a newly edited statement, the Department of Justice said on Friday that the U.S. Senate, the Federal Reserve, NASA and others were "among the targets of QTFY," a Chinese state-sponsored hacking group that officials identified on Wednesday during an internet domain seizure operation.
A previous version of the statement said the government agencies had been among the hackers' victims.
A note left at the bottom of the newly edited statement said that "Edits have been made to ensure this press release accurately reflects the government’s allegations in the affidavit in support of the domain seizures."
The DOJ said on Friday it made a correction to the press release because the August 26 release "described all agencies as victims whereas the government's affidavit made clear that all were targeted but only some were compromised."
The distinction matters because it narrows the scope of confirmed breaches in what the DOJ described as a years-long Chinese cyber-espionage campaign against U.S. government agencies, defense contractors and other sensitive targets.
AFFIDAVIT DETAILS TARGETS SINCE 2018 According to the FBI affidavit released alongside the original statement, since at least 2018 the hackers "targeted" U.S. federal networks including those of NASA, the Federal Reserve, the Department of Energy, the Department of Justice, the Department of Health and Human Services, the National Institutes of Health, and the U.S. Senate.
A footnote in the affidavit said that the FBI investigated the targeting of NASA and found that the attempted breach of NASA was unsuccessful due to the agency's patching of targeted software.
The affidavit alleges that in September 2024, the hackers carried out "computer intrusions" at three "DOE National Laboratories, NIH, an HHS agency, and a U.S. security device manufacturer," and referred to the entities as "victims."
A separate joint cybersecurity advisory issued by the FBI, National Security Agency and U.S. Cyber Command's Cyber National Mission Force published on Wednesday listed successful data thefts from unnamed defense contractors, financial institutions and universities in May 2024, and unsuccessful attempts to access networks of the U.S. Senate and a U.S. hospital in March 2026.
Messages seeking clarification from the FBI and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency were not immediately returned on Friday.
The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Friday. In response to Wednesday's announcement, an embassy spokesperson said the U.S. uses cybersecurity to "smear or discredit China" and that China "opposes the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security and using it as a pretext to impose discriminatory restrictions on Chinese companies and will firmly safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies."

items.title: Reds place 3B Ke'Bryan Hayes (groin) on injured list
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Reds placed struggling third baseman Ke'Bryan Hayes on the 10-day injured list Friday due to a left groin strain.
items.body:
The Reds placed struggling third baseman Ke'Bryan Hayes on the 10-day injured list Friday due to a left groin strain.
The move is retroactive to Thursday. In a corresponding transaction, Cincinnati recalled infielder Edwin Arroyo from Triple-A Louisville.
Hayes last played on Wednesday, going 1-for-4 in a 10-9 win at San Francisco. He was replaced by pinch hitter Tyler Stephenson in the ninth inning.
Hayes, 29, also was on the IL from May 21 to July 9 because of a bulging disc in his back.
He is batting a career-low .153 with five home runs and eight RBIs in 78 games. His .213 on-base percentage, .250 slugging percentage and .463 OPS also are career lows.
A Gold Glove winner in 2023 and 2025, Hayes is a career .245 hitter with 47 homers and 233 RBIs in 706 games for the Pittsburgh Pirates (2020-25) and Reds (2025-present). Pittsburgh selected Hayes in the first round (32nd overall) of the 2015 MLB Draft.
Arroyo, 23, has batted .244 (32-for-131) with five RBIs in 44 games since making his major league debut on June 1. He was hitting .309 with 15 homers and 43 RBIs in 72 games for Louisville.
--Field Level Media
